submissionAttempts.body:
The post-1.2.0 (ORD-BOOT-0 / 1.3.1) observation-cursor behaviour applies to this workspace's Palimpsest↔Ordarium integration; the 1.2.0-line behaviour does not.

Candidate behaviours:
- 1.2.0 line: docs/release-commentary-1.2.0.md — "predates the incremental state-change feed, so it has no notion of a change-feed cursor and no cursor-invalidation failure", explicitly self-scoped ("Anything here applies only to the 1.2.0 line") and marked "historical, superseded by later releases".
- Post-1.2.0: StateChangeFeed/StateStore.changes(filter?, cursor?) returns {changes, cursor, hasMore} with `cursor` always present — an opaque, filter-independent durable position. Decode is strict (base64url {"c":"<digits>"}), and the position is validated against the ledger-wide high-water mark: invalid/foreign/restored/replaced cursors throw InvalidCursorError and fail closed (no silent restart), while concurrent commits only raise the mark so valid cursors are never falsely rejected. Gated by the explicit LedgerCapabilities.stateChangeFeed + supportsStateChangeFeed, else LedgerCapabilityRequiredError.

Why: the operative integration is Ordarium 1.3.1, declared consistently by package.json (core/ledger-sqlite/host-kit/testing pinned to ordarium-v1.3.1 tarballs), pnpm-workspace.yaml overrides (same four URLs), and the installed node_modules artifacts (@ordarium/{core,host-kit,ledger-sqlite} package.json = 1.3.1; SqliteLedger/MemoryLedger both declare stateChangeFeed: true). docs/engineering/07-ordarium-alignment.md still records the 1.2.0 four-line pin (revision log ends at r19), so it is a stale record behind the code, not a competing behaviour definition. The 1.2.0 commentary is version-scoped, historical and superseded, so it cannot govern a 1.3.1 integration. Resolution is local (version scope + explicit supersession), so no peer contact is required.

Nuance: Palimpsest's current code consumes List's nextCursor pagination (telemetry load in src/telemetry/state_persistence.ts), not changes(); the change-feed observation cursor is exposed by the pinned integration surface but not yet called, so no existing call site is affected. Any state-change observation by this integration must use the 1.3.1 fail-closed cursor semantics above.
